_partNote: Every class here is a substance rather than a machine, so each tile draws the characteristic mill form instead: a structural section, an extruded profile, a molded part with pellets, a cured ring with a foam block, a brittle tile with a glass pane, a woven laminate panel, and a stack of magnetic laminations. The seven are told apart by silhouette (beam, chambered tube, tub, torus, flat tile, weave, comb) rather than by color or surface finish, which the shared two-color palette would flatten anyway.

partPrompts.1: A short length of wide-flange I-beam lying on a flat surface, seen three-quarter, with the H-shaped cross-section clearly visible at its cut end: two parallel flanges joined by one thin central web. Behind it lies a flat rectangular plate offcut with one irregular cut edge. The beam is the dominant object; not a solid block, no machine and no tooling.
partPrompts.2: A short length of hollow extruded profile standing upright on a flat surface, seen three-quarter, its open top end face showing the shape of the extrusion: a rectangular tube divided by two internal ribs into three long channels, with a T-slot groove running down the outside of each face. The intricate open end face is the subject. Not an I-beam, not a solid bar, no plate, no machine.
partPrompts.3: One thin-walled molded tub standing upright on a flat surface, seen three-quarter: a tapered open-topped container with a rolled rim and a few shallow vertical ribs down its sides, clearly thin in section where the rim is visible. In front of it, well separated, a small loose scatter of about a dozen short cylindrical pellets. The tub is the dominant object; no fabric, no weave, no foam, no machine.
partPrompts.4: A thick O-ring lying flat on a surface, seen three-quarter: a doughnut-shaped ring of round cross-section with a fat soft-looking profile, not a flat washer and not a thin annulus. Behind it, well separated, stands a rectangular block whose faces carry a coarse open-cell pore texture like a sponge. Two objects only, the ring dominant, on a plain surface with no machine and no tooling.
partPrompts.5: A square flat tile lying on a surface, seen three-quarter, with one corner broken cleanly away and the small triangular chip lying beside the gap, so the break reads as brittle rather than bent. Behind it, well separated, a thin flat rectangular pane stands on edge with its narrow edge thickness clearly visible and its face plain. The tile is dominant; no weave, no fibers, no machine.
partPrompts.6: A flat rectangular laminate panel lying on a surface, seen three-quarter, its top face covered in a coarse regular over-and-under woven pattern of wide flat tows. One corner is cut away in a clean step, and along that cut the panel edge shows about six thin plies stacked one on top of another. One object on a plain surface; not a smooth plate, no machine and no tooling.
partPrompts.7: A stack of E-shaped stampings assembled into a magnetic core, standing upright on a flat surface and seen three-quarter: three parallel limbs rising from one common back, with the many thin identical layers of the stack visible as fine lines along the top edges of the limbs. The comb-like E silhouette is the subject. Absolutely no wire, no windings, no coil, no bobbin, and no woven texture.
